# Independent audit of the all-dimensional mass-dependent centroid bound

Source audited:
`candidate 660db01ed45063dd`.
The ordinary inequality, all-dimensional scalar certificate, and
mixed coupling application PASS. The strict infimum assertion is valid;
a short uniform-gap justification, given below, has been sent to the
author for explicit inclusion.

## Measures, source, and scalar reduction

After scaling |K|=1, domination eta<=1_K dx gives alpha in[0,1],
absolute continuity, and a density for rho which is at least one.
The supporting-functional argument puts its actual centroid in int K.
For a nonconstant direction, the projected convex-body distribution
has a strictly positive continuous interior density (constant in d=1).
Thus V(X) is uniform and the pushed eta has density h in[0,1].

Cap-root concavity is applied in the correct direction at the actual
rho centroid. The two interval rearrangements preserve their separate
eta masses, and their intervals fit because r<=s and alpha-r<=1-s.
Writing q=1+1/d, the displayed equation(2) and substitution
U=1/s, E=r/s, Q=(s+alpha-r)/s give

    phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)>=2/(d+1)

exactly. All denominators are positive; no hidden density smoothness,
positive boundary mass, or exchange of unsigned integrals is needed.

## Dual objective and every dimension

With A=Gamma_d^(-1) and L=4A/3-1, the desired mass-dependent ratio is
exactly equivalent to D=U+Q-L E<1+4A/3. Applying the one-variable dual
bound with multipliers 1/d,1/(2d),-L/(2d) and multiplicities1,2,2
produces D/d as its linear term. Subtracting the scalar lower bound
therefore gives equation(6) with coefficient d/(d+1), as stated.
The difference from the required objective bound is precisely

    epsilon_d=d Delta_d/(d+1).

For d>=14 the derivative proof that (1+1/d)^d increases is correct.
I independently checked 8*15^14>21*14^14, the exponential-series upper
bound87/32<(33/20)^2, and the lower Taylor sum
2058029/589824>80/23. The first negative term is bounded using
(1+1/(2d))^d<sqrt(e), retaining its final factor1+1/(2d). The second
uses L>5/2. Their sum is less than31/8+33/(20d), whereas the positive
term is at least31/8+15/(8d). The coefficient gap is9/40>0.
Thus the proof is uniform over the entire infinite range d>=14.

For d=1,...,13 I parsed and recomputed every AppendixA integer. The
identities B/J=(2d+1)/(2d), N/J=1-L/(2d), and positive-term=2Z/J
prove the displayed formula for Delta. All thirteen N and all thirteen
listed R_d are strictly positive and match their defining integer
expressions exactly. Hence Delta=1/8+R_d/(8J^(d+1))>1/8 in those
dimensions. This is an exact finite part of a dimension-uniform proof,
not numerical evidence extrapolated to higher dimensions.

## Coupling and actual mixed point

The archived coupling, or the direct conditional-Fubini proof, provides
one measure eta of mass v dominated by ordinary volume and supported
in the actual midpoint body. Its first moment is v(g_A+g_B)/2. This
makes the rho centroid exactly the continuous coordinate of the true
mixed centroid, with integer coordinate zero; it is an actual point
of K. The pointwise closed-halfspace union inequality gives the bound
for every pair of endpoint affine offsets, so ambient oblique normals
are retained. Pure integer normals are treated separately and contain
the entire middle fiber plus an endpoint; no boundary mass is lost.

The claim that A,K,B are precisely the integer fibers of their convex
hull is valid: any convex combination at base zero has equal total
weights on the endpoint levels, and their midpoint body is contained
in K. At bases plus/minus one no other level can contribute. The hull
has nonempty ambient interior, since all bodies are full dimensional.

## Uniform strictness before taking the depth infimum

A strict inequality for each halfspace alone need not justify a strict
infimum. Here the source's actual dual gap supplies what is required.
Equation(6) and Delta_d>0 imply

    D<=1+4A/3-epsilon_d,    epsilon_d=d Delta_d/(d+1)>0.

Consequently

    s+r >= (3/(4A))(1+alpha+epsilon_d s).

Because g lies in int K, one fixed closed ball around g is contained
in K. Every ordinary halfspace through g contains half that ball, so
s has a uniform positive lower bound. Hence all the nonvertical ambient
caps have a common strictly positive mass gap above the claimed target.
The two pure integer caps also have a fixed positive gap. Taking the
infimum over all ambient halfspaces therefore retains strict inequality.
This argument should be stated explicitly alongside the notation
D_S(Y)> in the source. It needs no compactness or continuity assertion
at pure-integer normals.

The resulting theorem remains a particular three-fiber equal-endpoint
statement. It supplies no decomposition preserving global mass for
arbitrary mixed-integer bodies.

The independent exact checker is
`supporting computation verify_all_dimensional_mass_dependent_centroid_audit_defect_transport.py`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
